data.title: Arab Parliament Welcomes Support from 162 Countries for the Right of the Palestinian People to Self-Determination
data.content:
Cairo, November 20, 2026, SPA -- The Arab Parliament welcomed the adoption by the United Nations General Assembly, with the support of 162 countries, of the annual resolution reaffirming the inalienable right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and the establishment of their independent, sovereign state, while rejecting the continued Israeli occupation.
    In a statement issued today, the Arab Parliament stressed that the vote represents a new political and diplomatic victory for Palestinian rights and reflects broad international consensus on the legitimacy of these rights and the need to end the Israeli occupation. This is consistent with the advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice, which affirmed the illegality of Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territories and the need to end it as rapidly as possible.
    The Arab Parliament also welcomed the adoption by the General Assembly's Fourth Committee of three UN resolutions concerning the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA), Palestinian refugees' properties, and Israeli settlements. These resolutions reaffirm support for UNRWA's mandate, the protection of refugees' rights, particularly the rights to return and compensation, and the illegality of Israeli settlements and their violation of international law and UN resolutions.
    The Arab Parliament called on the international community to move beyond issuing resolutions and expressing positions toward taking practical steps and effective, binding international measures to ensure the effective implementation of these resolutions, protect UNRWA and ensure the continuation of its humanitarian operations, halt settlement activities, annexation, and forced displacement, end the Israeli occupation, and enable the Palestinian people to exercise their fundamental right to self-determination and establish their independent, sovereign state with Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with relevant resolutions of international legitimacy.
    -- SPA
